$comment: EXAMPLE provider table for delegated omp runs. Read by bin/omp-tab.sh (preflight and fallback). Replace the rows below with your own providers before launching anything real.

Adding a provider is one row under `providers`; a provider absent from the table is still probed, so an unknown one works before it is documented. Switching one off is `enabled: false`: an explicit --model on it is refused before any check, and the fallback walk skips it.

`check` is how omp-tab.sh proves the provider can serve before opening a tab. `probe` runs a one-word `omp -p` request on the model itself, which costs a few tokens. `balance` reads a prepaid balance endpoint, which costs nothing, and reports the figure and the top-up link.

`fallback` is the order tried when the model a launch resolves to cannot serve. omp itself never falls back across providers on a refused request, so this list is the only fallback that exists. The account default (modelRoles.default in the omp config file) is tried first whatever this list says; entries here are what comes after it.

`allowedModels` is the allowlist of models a tab may launch on. The EXAMPLE list holds the default model, the two fallback entries and one heavier model, so the fallback walk can launch when the default cannot serve; a model the walk may land on must be in this list or the walk is refused. omp-tab.sh refuses before launch when the resolved model is not in the list, and closes a tab whose session file shows it started on another. A missing key means no allowlist (a note says so). Replace it with your own list.

opencode-go.why: Example: subscription account with no key-based entitlement endpoint, so the only honest check is a real request.

deepseek.why: Example: prepaid direct account; an empty balance refuses every tab at once. The key comes from KEY_COMMAND (see bin/omp-tab.sh).
